slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you more
disciplined than 90% of men
Doing the boring task first. The email you avoid, the dishes, the report. Starting with what you don't want to do makes everything after it feel easy.
Going to bed at a fixed time. Not when the series ends, at your chosen hour. Discipline at night is what creates energy in the morning.
Training even when it's raining. Rain, cold, a long day at work. The workout you do on a bad day counts more than ten on perfect days, because it proves you show up no matter what.
Keeping promises to yourself. If you said you'd read tonight, you read. Every kept promise makes the next one easier to keep.
Learning every day without exception. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a small daily habit has trained my discipline more than any big goal.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A small daily habit trained my discipline more than any big goal.

slides.texte_overlay: Saying no to the extra drink, the extra episode, the extra scroll. Small refusals add up to a life that's actually under your control.
Planning tomorrow before you sleep. Three tasks written down. Waking up with a clear plan removes the excuses before they even start, and your morning runs itself.
